disposition_reason: Table 1 prints mean ± SEM lead and cadmium in raw and boiled chicken liver and meat from fresh and imported frozen birds, with an unresolved unit conflict.

study.design: 2 x 2 experiment: fresh versus imported frozen chicken, before versus after boiling; liver and meat
study.origin: fresh: chicks slaughtered locally; frozen: imported, different brands
study.market: local markets, Al-Karkh Province, Baghdad, Iraq
study.method: HNO3/HClO4 hot-plate digestion of 1 g wet tissue; graphite furnace AAS (Shimadzu AA-7000)
study.qa: four-point calibration from 1000 mg/L standards; no CRM, blank or recovery reported

findings.group: fresh chicken, slaughtered locally, Al-Karkh, Baghdad; uncooked
findings.integrity_flag: Table unit ppm (mg/kg) implies lead of 80-420 mg/kg and cadmium of 24-163 mg/kg in chicken tissue, which cannot be reconciled with graphite-furnace AAS food analysis or with ordinary poultry levels; the unit may be µg/kg. Value not converted.
findings.notes: Mean ± SEM (SEM 19.41), n = 10 per group; wet weight basis. Printed value 84.20 ppm kept verbatim; value_ugkg left null because of the unit conflict.

controls.control: boiling 25-30 min in tap water (metal pan)
controls.outcome: Liver Pb fresh 84.20 -> 79.50, frozen 89.69 -> 321.8 (printed ppm; cooking p=0.017, interaction p=0.013); meat Pb fresh 215.8 -> 245.4, frozen 421.6 -> 324.4 (p=0.834); liver Cd fresh 144.3 -> 162.9, frozen 72.11 -> 88.40 (p=0.665); meat Cd fresh 127.8 -> 133.7, frozen 51.90 -> 24.30 (p=0.731). Units as printed; see integrity flag.

controls.control: storage: imported frozen versus fresh chicken
controls.outcome: main-effect means liver Pb 81.85 (fresh) vs 205.7 (frozen), p=0.009; meat Cd 130.8 vs 38.10, p=0.005 (printed ppm)

unresolved: Table 1 unit label ppm is implausible for the magnitudes (lead up to 421.6 and cadmium up to 162.9 'ppm' in chicken); the true unit (possibly µg/kg) cannot be confirmed, so no µg/kg values are stored.
Main-effect marginal means (Table 1 lower panel) are pooled across the same samples and recorded only in controls.
Sampling dates not reported; boiling water and pan metal were not analysed, so the increase after boiling cannot be attributed.
Boiling water (broth) itself was not analysed; meat and liver only.
